summary: Iteration 46 — WhatsApp Smart Capture (Phase 1) end-to-end validation. Backend pytest 15/15 PASS: /api/whatsapp/status + owner-only /api/whatsapp/logs (403 for non-owner), inbound webhook (localhost:8001) creates capture drafts via AI triage (sales, invoice, meeting, and high-value >=50000 escalated correctly with needs_owner=true), GET /api/captures with role-based visibility (owner sees all, sales sees only reviewer_role=sales), GET /api/captures/pending-count, PATCH edit, /reassign, /clarify (moves to clarification_requested), /reject (moves to rejected), /approve (executes → creates a decision, status→executed, result_ref populated), and 403 when a non-owner tries to approve a needs_owner=true draft. Frontend Playwright: owner login → sidebar 'Review Queue' with pending-count badge → /review page renders 4 status tabs and all pending cards with classification/reviewer/priority chips + escalation warning + all 5 action buttons; approving a non-escalated card synchronously executes and the card moves from Pending → Approved (executed) tab. No auto-execution observed anywhere.

issues: Notification bell badge showed '180' — larger than the 20px pill can visually cap without overflow; consider capping display as '99+' for readability (unrelated to this iteration but visible while testing).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 4302 lines — WhatsApp + Smart Capture (~700 lines from 3590→4038) is a self-contained slice ideal for extraction into routers/whatsapp.py and routers/captures.py. Continues the same file-size concern flagged in iteration 44/45.

persist_capture_draft() forces reviewer_role='owner' when the routed department doesn't exist as a tenant role (line 3862-3863). For tenants without a 'finance' role, all invoice/payment drafts pile onto the owner. Consider surfacing this in the UI (e.g. a warning banner 'invoice drafts have no finance reviewer configured — routing to owner') or letting the tenant map classifications→roles in settings.

ai_capture_triage() has no timeout/retry on the LLM call. If the LLM stalls or returns malformed JSON the fallback is 'other'+medium priority — which is safe, but a stale/hanging LLM call blocks the background task and blocks the sender's confirmation reply. Consider wrapping in asyncio.wait_for(…, timeout=20).

CAPTURE_ROUTING (line 3802) hard-codes 'operations' as a possible department in the LLM prompt (line 3817) but 'operations' is not in the routing map and not part of the Sharma demo roles (sales/production/finance). The fallback re-routes to owner cleanly, but tightening the LLM prompt roles to the actual tenant roles would produce fewer owner-escalations for large tenants.

reject_capture stores the reason under 'clarification_note' (line 4007) — same field used by clarify. That's a naming collision and shows up in the UI as 'Note: <reject reason>' on rejected rows. Consider a separate 'rejection_reason' field.

The Approve action on the Review Queue synchronously waits for execute_capture → process_voice_note → LLM extraction, which took ~5-6s in the test. The FE has no loading indicator on the Approve button beyond a disabled state. Consider adding a spinner + 'Executing…' label; and possibly enqueue this as a background task and use polling like voice_notes so the button feels snappy.

The FE Captures page uses window.prompt() for reassign role, reject reason, and clarify note (Captures.js lines 111-122). This is jarring and inconsistent with the rest of the app (shadcn dialogs). Same UX concern raised in iteration 45 for task rejection.

ROLE_OPTS in Captures.js is hard-coded to ['sales','finance','purchase','hr','operations','owner'] instead of using the tenant's actual roles list from AuthContext.tenant.roles. On a tenant with custom roles ('production' etc.), reassignment via the built-in dropdown/prompt suggests roles the tenant doesn't have.
No pagination on GET /api/captures (to_list(100)) — will silently drop older drafts on a busy tenant. Add limit/offset.

GET /api/captures response doesn't currently include reviewer_role's members list, so the FE loads /api/users separately every time the Edit form opens. Fine for now, but a single joined response would remove a round-trip.
action_items: (Enhancement) Add a rejection_reason field distinct from clarification_note (currently overloaded).
(Enhancement) Replace window.prompt() usage in Captures.js with shadcn Dialog for reassign / reject / clarify (consistency with rest of app).
(Enhancement) Drive ROLE_OPTS from tenant.roles instead of a hard-coded list.
(Enhancement) Add loading indicator on Approve button while execute_capture runs (~5-8s).
(Enhancement) Continue server.py extraction — move captures + whatsapp into their own routers.

seed_data_creation: Sent 8 synthetic WhatsApp text webhooks (all prefixed TEST_CAP_*): TEST_CAP_SALES, TEST_CAP_INVOICE, TEST_CAP_HIGHVAL, TEST_CAP_MEETING, TEST_CAP_ACTIONS_<ts>, TEST_CAP_REJECT_<ts>, TEST_CAP_APPROVE_<ts>, TEST_CAP_OWNER_ONLY_<ts>. All landed in the WA_TENANT_ID Sharma workspace via resolve_wa_tenant fallback. One draft was approved (creates a decision + tasks in Sharma tenant), one moved to clarification_requested, one to rejected. Remaining drafts left pending for main-agent visibility. UI also approved 1 additional non-escalated draft.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 46 WhatsApp Smart Capture (Phase 1) is fully working end-to-end. Key rules to preserve: (1) POST /api/webhooks/whatsapp NEVER auto-creates a decision/task — it only stores a capture_draft with status='pending_review'. (2) resolve_wa_tenant matches on invited_employees[].phone (last-10-digits) and falls back to WA_TENANT_ID env; the Sharma demo tenant WA_TENANT_ID=ae79cf8b-... is set so any sender is routed to Sharma unless matched to another tenant. (3) needs_owner is set when classification in (approval, decision), OR amount >= CAPTURE_THRESHOLD (50000 INR), OR policy_or_high_risk=true from the LLM. (4) POST /api/captures/{id}/approve is SYNCHRONOUS — it runs execute_capture which awaits process_voice_note (LLM call) → creates a decision + unblocked tasks and returns the result_ref. On the FE this is a 5-8s wait. (5) POST from Python must go to http://localhost:8001 not the external URL (Cloudflare WAF returns 403 for non-browser UAs on the webhook path). (6) reject/clarify both write to 'clarification_note' field — this is currently overloaded (minor concern flagged for main agent). (7) The FE nav badge (nav-review-badge) uses /api/captures/pending-count with refetchInterval=30s; the Review Queue itself refetches every 20s.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. All 15 backend tests and 5 UI checkpoints passed.
